title: Trump is set to redefine the lame duck presidency
gist: Chatham House argues that although Republicans lost both houses of Congress in the 2026 midterms over petrol prices, the economy and a nine-month Iran war, Trump will not become a constrained lame duck. Having already issued 292 executive orders, he will route AI, immigration, energy and deregulation policy through executive action, veto a polarized Congress that may constrain itself, and chase a legacy endgame via Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi and possibly renewed military action against Iran.

themes.theme: Midterm rebuke over petrol, economy and Iran

insights.claim: Republicans lost control of both houses of Congress in the 2026 midterms, which voters treated as a referendum on Trump, signalling disapproval of petrol prices, the state of the US economy and the war with Iran.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Cost-of-living and energy prices are the binding political constraint; expect policy reflexes aimed at pump prices through 2028.
insights.quote: They don’t approve of the cost of petrol at the pump, they don’t approve of the state of the US economy, and they don’t approve of the war with Iran.
insights.locator: Although Donald Trump’s name was not on any ballot

insights.claim: Trump ignored Republican hopes that he would focus on affordability before the midterms, instead picking a poorly understood fight with Canada and failing to find an exit from a Middle East conflict that drove up global energy prices.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Geopolitical distraction translated directly into an energy-price shock and electoral loss — energy price is the transmission channel to watch.
insights.quote: He picked a fight with Canada that very few at home understood.

insights.claim: Before the midterms Trump struck a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy millions of tons of Russian diesel, ostensibly to relieve domestic energy costs, a move the author says befuddled many.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A US-Russia diesel channel is a notable sanctions/energy-flow anomaly with implications for distillate markets and transatlantic alignment.
insights.quote: reached a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to purchase millions of tons of Russian diesel
insights.locator: He picked a fight with Canada

insights.claim: The Iran war, now nearly nine months into what was intended as a multiweek operation, may by itself have cost Republicans the midterms.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Mission creep in Iran is a sustained energy-risk premium driver and a political liability that shapes the remaining two years.
insights.quote: Nearly nine months into an intended multiweek operation, the realities of a war that may alone have cost Republicans the midterms are not favourable.
insights.locator: Trump is also desperate to manufacture

insights.claim: Contrary to conventional wisdom that losing both chambers hampers a second-term president, the author argues Trump will not recede and will redefine the lame-duck presidency.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Do not price a policy-quiet lame duck; executive-driven policy volatility likely persists to 2028.
insights.quote: Like so many facets of American politics over the past decade, Trump is set to redefine the lame duck presidency.
insights.locator: We should not expect Trump to recede

insights.claim: Historical precedent shows divided government curbs second-term agendas: Bush and Obama both saw immigration reform fail before hostile congresses, and Trump's first-term border wall, infrastructure and immigration plans stalled after Democrats won the House in 2018.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Legislative ambitions requiring Congress are now effectively dead; only executive-action channels remain live.

insights.claim: Democrats plan to use power of the purse, approval of presidential appointments and investigations to slow Trump, but the record is mixed: Republicans blocked Merrick Garland and extracted spending concessions via the debt ceiling under Biden, while the Trump and Clinton impeachments ended without conviction.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Appropriations and the debt ceiling are the real leverage points — watch funding deadlines for fiscal brinkmanship and market volatility.
insights.quote: both the Trump and Clinton impeachment efforts demonstrated there are limits to the bite of congressional oversight

insights.claim: Democrats may launch new impeachment investigations, including against Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, but lack the two-thirds Senate majority for conviction, and a quarter of polled Americans think renewed impeachment would embolden Trump and make him more popular.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Impeachment is noise rather than a policy-changing event; it may even strengthen the president's hand.
insights.quote: a quarter of those polled believe that renewed impeachment efforts will embolden the president and make him more popular

insights.claim: Extreme polarization means Americans no longer share facts and politicians no longer cooperate, making a veto-proof supermajority unlikely, so with Trump positioning as 'Mr. Veto' the new Congress may end up constraining itself rather than the president.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Expect legislative gridlock plus unchecked executive action — the worst mix for policy predictability.
insights.quote: Rather than constraining the president, the next Congress may therefore end up constraining itself.
insights.locator: Despite the best intentions of the founding fathers

themes.theme: Executive-order governance as the main channel

insights.claim: Drawing on first-term experience and the Project 2025 agenda, Trump's second-term strategy was to lean on executive authority, use Congress selectively and shrug off legal challenges, starting with a 'flood the zone' approach of two dozen executive orders on day one.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: The governing model already assumes a hostile or irrelevant Congress, so losing it changes less than headlines imply.
insights.quote: Trump’s plan was always to lean heavily on his executive authority, to rely only selectively on Congress, and to be undeterred by inevitable legal challenges.
insights.locator: That experience informed the Project 2025 agenda

insights.claim: Over his second term Trump has issued 292 executive orders, 90 memoranda and 192 proclamations, after passing priorities such as the One Big Beautiful Bill, the Laken Riley Act and the Secure America Act through a Republican Congress.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: The pace of executive action is the metric to track for regulatory risk across sectors.
insights.quote: the president has issued 292 executive orders , 90 memoranda and 192 proclamations
insights.locator: Over the course of his second term

insights.claim: Trump's remaining domestic priorities on artificial intelligence, immigration, deregulation and energy will be funnelled through executive action in his final two years.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: AI, energy and deregulation policy will keep moving via executive orders — sector exposure to executive-action and litigation risk stays high.
insights.quote: including on artificial intelligence, immigration, deregulation, and energy – will be funnelled through the president’s office
insights.locator: Over the course of his second term

insights.claim: With the midterms behind him, Trump's overriding priority is his legacy, including his claim to have ended eight long-standing conflicts, monuments in Washington, remaking the White House ballroom and winning the Nobel Peace Prize.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Legacy-seeking raises the odds of dramatic, deal-driven foreign-policy moves that can move markets abruptly.
insights.quote: However, Trump’s greatest goal is securing his legacy.

insights.claim: Trump's second term has replaced ideology with transactionalism and consultation with unilateralism, through reciprocal tariffs, treating Canada and Mexico as adversaries, Greenland takeover talk that roiled markets, flattering Xi Jinping and chastising Zelenskyy.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Alliance and trade relationships remain transactional and reversible — a persistent geopolitical risk premium for allied economies.
insights.quote: Trump replaced ideology with transactionalism, and consultation with unilateralism.
insights.locator: During his second term, the president has sought

insights.claim: Frustrated at failing to broker a lasting Ukraine ceasefire, Trump has swung back toward Putin, viewing the war as about access, energy, critical minerals and proximity to power, and is pinning hopes on planned trilateral meetings in Abu Dhabi.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A Russia-leaning settlement push is a key swing factor for European energy, defence and Ukraine-reconstruction assets; Abu Dhabi talks are the near-term catalyst.
insights.quote: For Trump the war is about access, energy and critical mineral resources, and proximity to power.

insights.claim: With diplomacy on Iran stalled and economic leverage slow, there are growing signs the US and Israel may soon renew military action, and Trump will be tempted to try kinetic conflict again in pursuit of victory regardless of the midterm result.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Renewed strikes on Iran would re-escalate oil and energy prices — keep an energy-risk hedge despite the political cost already incurred.
insights.quote: In his quest for victory, he will be tempted to give kinetic conflict another try.
insights.locator: With diplomacy stalled and economic leverage

insights.claim: The author concludes Trump will not let domestic politics, divided government or the US political system constrain his legacy pursuit, intending to 'fly like a free bird, not sink like a lame duck.'
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Base case for 2027-28 is continued high-variance policy from the White House, not paralysis.
insights.quote: Trump intends to fly like a free bird, not sink like a lame duck.
